chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Charlie Hite, the Apex Club and Sheffield's Last Round-Up
summary: Spikes does not know a Charlie Hite, recalls the name Apex, and says Sheffield ran the Last Round-Up on Thirty-Eighth and Central around 1932-33.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: It says, "Chicago Defender story...21st April 1928 edition said that Charlie Hite was with Mosby."
Well, that might have been. I don't know no Charlie Hite.
I don't either. And, the band at the Apex Club...that's right, the place that was later the Alabam was once the Apex, right? Or, no. There were two Apexes, weren't there? On Central Avenue?
I don't remember. I know I remember the name Apex but I don't remember who ran it.
Old Sheffield had a nightclub there on Thirty-Eighth and Central, too, called Round-Up...Last Round-Up.
[Laughing] That's a great name for Sheffield's.
Yeah, it was called the Last Round-Up. He was mixed up in that.
What year was that? Was that after he left the Police Force?
That was about '32 or '33 somewhere in there.
That was after he left the Police Force?
